runs.question: What penalty does the NIST AI RMF set for an organization that chooses not to adopt it?

answer.text:
The NIST AI RMF does not set a penalty for organizations that decline to adopt it. The framework is designed as a voluntary resource, and I found no passage describing any sanction for non-adoption. The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, and use-case agnostic, providing flexibility to organizations of all sizes and in all sectors and throughout society to implement the approaches in the Framework.

The document also says the framework is a resource that organizations can draw on. The goal of the AI RMF is to offer a resource to the organizations designing, developing, deploying, or using AI systems to help manage the many risks of AI and promote trustworthy and responsible development and use of AI systems.

Note that this answer covers only the AI RMF itself (NIST AI 100-1). Other documents in the collection, such as the OMB memos, may impose requirements on federal agencies, but I did not check them for this question.
